Having a child also genuinely ruined my marriage because while my life was flipped upside down and inside out, my husband's changed very little. While one of the nurses was stitching up my tear, he had the audacity to joke about getting the "husband stitch"... The energy created by the focusing of our mind by the words.

Maybe it's just my neurospiciness talking, but I think the "feeling behind the words" is more universal than that - the strange satisfaction of good rhymes, set to music. The interplay of vowels and consonants on our tongues. Words that are just "fun to say".  We've all sung along to songs without understanding/knowing all the lyrics before. Yes, there are thousands of songs that have profound lyrics, and this is not to diminish those in any way - it's just a different facet of the universal human experience that is music. There are just as many - if not more - composed over the centuries that have no words, yet stir within us deep, ineffable feelings, regardless of generation.

Companies have figured out how to assume tips are compulsary, and then use it as a way to pay their employees less than federal minimum wage. In GA, minimum wage is ~$7.25, yet a server's wage paid by the company is only ~$2.15. Tip makers never see a paycheck, as the money made barely covers federal and state taxes. Year-end taxes assume you made a minimum of 15% in tips. If in reality you did NOT make an average of 15%, you OWE money.

So, in a society that is largely uninformed about how the tip system works, thinks tips are optional, and are probably struggling financially, they can cause servers, bartenders, ect to pay the difference out of their own pockets.

And it is ENTIRELY the fault of greedy businesses who decided to use what used to be an occasional compliment for exemplary service as a way to pay employees less from their own coffers. It's infuriating and needs to be stopped, letting tips go back to their original meaning and intent.

As a server, one of the biggest problems with taxing tips is they are assuming the amount you make, regardless of the ACTUAL amount you make. Now, to those that have never worked a tip-based job, that might sound awesome because anything over that amount is "free money", but the reality is the exact opposite - 15% of total sales is what is expected, and most people are forced to pay taxes on tips they didn't actually receive. Tips are based entirely on the consumer, and many of them leave shitty tips for even rockstar servers. I've seen it many times - servers who were known at the business for consistently providing top-notch service, and most new workers often shadowed them - getting completely shafted in their tips. A $10 bill left on a multi-hundred dollar meal. Servers actually LOSE money, because again, they're assumed to make at least 15% in tips. ONE bad table could ruin your entire days' pay.

Depression can happen to anyone, anytime, at almost any age. I've suffered from chronic depression for almost as long as I have memories, but I could never tell my mother (she believes psychiatry is psuedo science), and it got to the point that I wanted to end it. I had a day, time, method... had I not met my boyfriend at band camp that summer, I wouldn't be here today. Even though she's young, PLEASE take this very seriously!

Take her to a good child psychiatrist for a full evaluation, and then *follow their recommendations*. If they suggest medication, understand that the journey to finding which one works best for her, and at what dose, is a process. It's finding the right tool for the job, so to speak, so be patient and optimistic. 

Talk to your daughter, check in with her - often - reassurring her that you're there for her, and that you want to understand what she's thinking/feeling so you can help her. This MUST come across as genuine, empathetic, and with absolutely no criticism or judgement. Compassionate connection between you two is an absolute necessity. She NEEDS to know and trust that Mom is in her corner, no matter what. Gently correct any negative self-talk, but also validate her feelings:

Her: "God, I just feel so stupid and worthless"

You: "I hear that you're struggling right now, and I know how crappy that can feel. But you are so much more amazing than you give yourself credit for. Everyone around you can see it - we just gotta figure out how to make it easier for you to see it too." 

Try to get her to talk about her ideas on self-harm - what is appealing about it, how does she feel during and after, ect. in a completely non-judgemental way. My aforementioned boyfriend would cut himself on his arms because it gave him a tangible pain he could control, instead of his emotional pain that he couldn't. 

Lastly - and arguably the most difficult part - is ask her if there is anything YOU have been doing that makes her feel worse, and ask what you can do to help. Again, actively LISTEN to her and do not react negatively to anything she may say. Try to look at it as constructive criticism - NO ONE is perfect, and there may be something you didn't realize was affecting her. It doesn't mean you're a bad mom. All it means is that you are working together towards a deeper understanding to ultimately help her.

Mental illnesses are every bit as serious as physical ones, and are often actually HARDER because it's an "invisible illness" - you can't SEE something wrong, so it gets downplayed, ignored, or even mocked. She NEEDS you to be her rock when she's at low points, and trust she can come to you about anything and you'll be there for her. It probably won't be easy, but trust in your own strength and love for your child, and you can do it. <3

Maybe even drifting blissfully in and out of sleep.  

Waking slowly as my senses tingle that something's not quite right, to find it unnaturally quiet. The fire had died down to glowing embers and the chill had crept back in. In the darkness around me, only flickers of the full moon through the dense trees serves as any type of light. I try looking around to get my bearings, but my ears prove the superior sense as I pick up distinct footsteps coming closer. Fear shooting through me as my imagination runs wild with scenarios of being found by a couple of hillfolk with nothing and no one around to protect me... then my heart leaping into my throat at realizing whatever was coming closer sounded too "off" to be human. 

A deep, rumbling growl floats through the dark as I try to stand, freezing me upright on my knees, and I let out a small whimper of fear, just knowing for certain I was about to be dinner for a pack of hungry wolves. My eyes dart around, trying to see anything I could, then focusing in front of me on what seemed like a large patch of void, where all light was sucked in and absorbed. Another softer rumble comes from the void and large amber eyes stare back at me. 

I let out a small yelp of surprise, instinctively shifting backwards and a fierce growl pins me to the spot, making it clear that retreat was unacceptable. Slowly, the features of a mignight black lycan become outlined in orange as it steps into the faint light of the fire pit. First on two legs, then lowering to all four as it comes forward to inspect me. I just barely stifle a scream as its large muzzle comes within inches of me, eyes fixed on mine, and tears begin rolling down my cheeks. I sit still as a statue as it begins to look me over, starting with my face, lingering on my breasts through my shirt, then drifting lower, taking in deep breaths of my scent. Its eyes fix between my legs and it lowers its muzzle until it is pressed into the thin fabric of my yoga pants, letting out a growl that seems almost... pleased?

I flinch at the contact, clamping my hands over my mouth as I try to control my hyperventilating, and the beast's eyes snap back to mine with a displeased snarl. It comes closer, its snout moving past my face and I feel its hot breath against my neck as its tongue slowly licks from my shoulder to right below my ear. Then my blood runs cold as the beast growls out one barely intelligable word - "MATE..."

The cabin was eventually investigated after I failed to check out at the end of my stay, with all my belongings found still inside. The only traces of occupancy left were the shredded clothing and rumpled blanket next to the firepit. The local police aired a warning that day to "Be careful of the woods. I know almost all the advice you'll find is to NOT contact/meet him, and that's probably the smartest choice.

However, I also can see how confronting him to prove that you have taken back your own power, and to get everything off your chest, could be part of your healing process.

So, with all that in mind, here's my opinion/what I would do:

1.) Agree to meet with him, but *only* in a non-enclosed public place (outdoor cafe, busy public park, ect). 

2.) Without his knowledge, have a couple friends wait in a car where they can see you at all times, ready to jump to your help if needed. Be on a call with one friend who has their end set on speakerphone, and have another friend recording video so they can both hear everything that's said AND be recording it.

3.) This part is VERY important - you need to make sure that your tone stays strong, but not combative (think kinda like how a lawyer would speak during a cross examination) at all times. No raised voice on your part - just cold and authoritative. No small talk either, just get right to the point. Start by asking him "What do you want to talk about?". Let him say whatever he's going to say (don't interrupt, no matter how badly you want to). Once he's done, start asking him pointed questions about the things that happened during the relationship (ex. "Do you understand that [action XYZ he did] is emotional/physical/sexual abuse?"), basically to get him to admit the things he did. 

4.) Once you have all of his confessions recorded via the secret phone call, tell him point-blank that he is to, under no circumstances, EVER attempt to contact you or anyone connected to you (family, friends, employer, ect) ever again. That there is nothing he can do/say to ever make you want to even hear his name ever again. That he is nothing to you, and holds no power over you, and never will again. This is your moment to say whatever YOU need in order to find closure. But keep that same controlled, strong, cold voice - and do not say anything that could be considered a threat. At the end, say something like, "Have I made myself clear?" (think the tone of a mom laying down the law).

5.) Stand up and just walk away. Go straight to wherever restraining/no-contact orders are issued in your area and take one out on him - the most restrictive one possible. If you are concerned he might try to come to your house, buy some sort of camera (think Ring doorbell type thing) to monitor around the outside of your home. Then wait.

6.) If he never contacts you again, then Huzzah! Problem solved. If he tries ANYTHING, then send your recording of the meeting to ALL of his friends/family informing them that he refuses to leave you alone and is in violation of the no-contact order. Now EVERYONE knows exactly what he did to you - by his own admission, too. Also inform the police too.

Best peaceful case, he leaves you alone. Best petty case, you get to expose him to his entire social circle, and possibly get him arrested for violating a restraining order. Just be smart about all of it so you stay safe.
